newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Akbank to pay dividend, up capital.
newsitem.headline: Turk Akbank to pay dividend, up capital.

text.p: Akbank T.A.S., one of Turkey's biggest private banks, said it would pay a 1,200 lira cash dividend per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share from its 1996 profits.
In a statement sent to the Istanbul Stock Exchange, Akbank said the dividend payout totalling 21.6 trillion lira would begin on April 9, 1997.
It said a capital increase was also approved at the bank's annual meeting of directors and shareholders.
The capital will be raised to 50 trillion lira from 18 trillion by issuing one right and 0.7777 bonus for one existing share after approval by the regulatory Capital Markets Board.
The bank posted 37.76 trillion lira of net profits in 1996, up 157 percent from 14.70 trillion a year ago.
Its deposits stood at 334.1 trillion lira and loans at 142.5 trillion lira at the end of 1996, more than doubling from 1995's 154.4 trillion and 54.4 trillion lira, respectively.
The bank is largely owned by the Sabanci group which is one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates.
